30.text: BAGS. — The bags for storing food usually

31.text: consist, in the case of the Maritime Chukchee, of a

32.text: complete seal-skin, with all the natural openings

33.text: carefully sewed up. A rip across the breast forms

34.text: the mouth of the bag. This kind of bag is used for

35.text: several purposes, — for floats of harpoon-lines, for

36.text: holding putrid meat for dog-food, etc. The inland

37.text: reindeer-breeders, who have little seal-skin, make

38.text: storage-bags out of old reindeer-skins, but always

39.text: give them an oblong form with a mouth across the middle. These bags are

40.text: usually so large that a single bag filled with putrid meat, or with blood

41.text: mixed with pounded leaves, forms a sledge-load for one reindeer.

42.text: Similar bags (Fig. 115) are used for storing clothes and old scraps of skin.

43.text: The flat narrow pillow-bag of the movable sleeping-room has a similar shape.
